# Gandhārajātaka (Ja 406)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Gandhārajātaka* (Ja 406; PTS Jā iii 363–368) is a birth story preserved in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral; Horner, Vinaya Pitaka; Hazra 1994]. According to the traditional nidāna, the Buddha delivered the story while residing at Jetavana in connection with the Vinaya rule governing the storing up of medicinal foods (Nissaggiya Pācittiya 23) [SuttaCentral; Horner, Vinaya Pitaka].
The narrative recounts a previous life in which the Bodhisatta and the future Ānanda were both kings who relinquished their royal wealth and abdicated to live as wandering ascetics [Anandajoti 2010; Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. When the former king (the Bodhisatta's companion) secretly stored a small quantity of salt to season his meals, the Bodhisatta admonished him for hoarding provisions after having renounced an entire kingdom [Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. The ascetic took offense, which prompted a discourse on humility, discipline, and being amenable to admonition [Anandajoti 2010; Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. Its opening verse observes that without innate wisdom or well-trained discipline (*vinaya*), human beings wander blindly like buffaloes in a forest [Anandajoti 2010; Hazra 1994].
SuttaCentral indexes four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies 27 Pali-internal text-reuse alignments, consisting primarily of extensive matches with the *Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as shared verses with the *Nīti-gantha-saṅgaho Naradakkhadīpanī* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records low-scoring automated alignments with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and the Tibetan *Mahāvyutpatti* (D 4346), though these represent machine text-reuse matches rather than established narrative parallels [DharmaNexus].

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0201a) (§2.2–6.1 ↔ §2752–2763); Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§5.4–7.4 ↔ §3341_4–3347); Nīti-gantha-saṅgaho Naradakkhadīpanī (Anya E1009n) (§4.1–4.4 ↔ §473–478)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): 雜阿含經 (ZH_T02_0099) [zh]; བྱེ་བྲག་ཏུ་རྟོགས་པར་བྱེད་པ། ([vyutpatti]) (D4346) [bo]
